item.title: Ten years later, LIGO is a black-hole hunting machine

item.title: Gravitational wave detectors can now ‘autotune’ their signals
item.description: The LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA (LVK) detector network has a new trick up its sleeve to improve the instruments’ sensitivity to gravitational waves: it’s called Astrophysical Calibration and it plays a role similar to auto-tune in music production. item.title: GWTC-4.0: New catalog more than doubles the number of gravitational-wave detections made by LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA observatories
item.description: This story first appeared on MIT News. The latest crop of space-time wobbles includes a variety of heavy, fast-spinning, and lopsided colliding black holes. item.title: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration successfully wraps up its fourth Observing Run
item.description: Today, the international LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration celebrates the successful completion of its fourth observing run (O4), marking another major step forward in the exploration of the gravitational wave universe. item.title: Luminosity-weighted galaxy and gravitational wave cross-correlations
item.description: arXiv:2610.32436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cross-correlations of galaxies and gravitational waves (GW) can be used to extract cosmological parameters and the gravitational wave bias. In this work, we study how to include galaxy luminosities in these spatial cross-correlations, inspired by the standard approach of dark sirens line-of-sight redshift priors. item.title: GWTC-5.0: Updated LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA Catalog sets new records in precision gravitational wave astronomy
item.description: The LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA Collaboration released today a new catalog of gravitational wave events.
